B: Inhibition of NKCC1 restores hyperpolarizing GABAergic inhibition, reducing corticospinal hyperexcitability in ALS
C: Reduction of muscle spasticity and slowing of motor function decline
statement: Repurposing the loop diuretic bumetanide for ALS could counteract motor neuron excitotoxicity by downregulating intracellular chloride and restoring inhibitory GABAergic tone.

B: Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibition enhances locus coeruleus-derived noradrenergic input to spinal motor neurons, upregulating BDNF-TrkB signalling
C: Preservation of motor unit integrity and delayed loss of muscle strength
statement: Atomoxetine, an ADHD drug, may slow ALS progression by boosting norepinephrine-mediated neurotrophic support to vulnerable motor neurons.

B: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism in microglia suppresses NLRP3 inflammasome priming and IL-1β release
C: Attenuation of neuroinflammation-driven motor neuron death, particularly in female ALS patients
statement: The progestin drospirenone, used in oral contraceptives, could be repositioned for ALS to target microglial mineralocorticoid receptor-driven neuroinflammation.

B: Moderate inhibition of lysosomal V-ATPase lowers lysosomal pH within an optimal range to enhance autophagic degradation of TDP-43 aggregates
C: Reduced cytoplasmic TDP-43 inclusion burden and delayed motor symptom onset
statement: The proton-pump inhibitor esomeprazole may promote clearance of pathological TDP-43 by fine-tuning lysosomal acidification and autophagy.

B: Gut-selective antibiotic reshapes microbiota composition, lowering systemic lipopolysaccharide and neurotoxic bile acid levels that activate CNS inflammatory pathways
C: Reduction of peripheral and central neuroinflammation, slowing functional decline
statement: Rifaximin, a non-absorbable antibiotic for gut infections, could attenuate ALS neuroinflammation by eliminating bacterial sources of pro-inflammatory mediators.

B: Opening of mitochondrial ATP-sensitive potassium channels improves mitochondrial bioenergetics and calcium handling in motor neurons
C: Preservation of diaphragmatic and limb muscle function, delaying respiratory failure
statement: The cardiac calcium sensitizer and mitoKATP opener levosimendan may protect dying motor neurons by stabilizing mitochondrial energy production in ALS.

B: Restoration of astrocytic glutamate transporter GLT-1 expression combined with mild NMDA receptor antagonism counteracts excitotoxic glutamate spillover
C: Decreased motor neuron excitotoxic injury and extended survival
statement: Acamprosate, an anti-craving drug, may redress glutamate homeostasis in ALS by both boosting astrocytic reuptake and tempering NMDA receptor overactivation.

B: Dual angiotensin II type 1 receptor blockade and partial PPARγ activation jointly suppress NADPH oxidase-driven oxidative stress and NF-κB-mediated inflammation
C: Attenuation of motoneuronal oxidative injury and glial reactivity
statement: Telmisartan’s unique dual action could provide a combinational neuroprotective approach against both oxidative and inflammatory arms of ALS pathogenesis.

B: Na/K-ATPase-mediated Src kinase inhibition suppresses astrocytic IL-6 and TNF-α release, reducing motor neuron inflammatory microenvironment
C: Decreased surrounding glial toxicity and improved motor neuron survival
statement: The cardiac glycoside digoxin could be redirected to ALS by dampening astrocyte-derived neurotoxic cytokine secretion via the Na/K-ATPase signalosome.

B: 5-HT2A receptor antagonism prevents serotonin-induced microglial activation and platelet pro-inflammatory mediator release
C: Reduced microglia-driven neuroinflammation and motor neuron damage
statement: Sarpogrelate, a 5-HT2A antagonist used for peripheral artery disease, may mitigate ALS neuroinflammation by blocking serotonin-mediated microgliosis.

B: Inhibition of microtubule-dependent NLRP3 inflammasome assembly and ASC speck formation blocks IL-1β/IL-18 maturation
C: Lessened inflammasome-driven neuroinflammation and delayed disease acceleration
statement: Colchicine, a long-used gout therapy, could be repurposed to suppress the NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation observed in ALS microglia.

B: Inhibition of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase reduces de novo pyrimidine synthesis, curtailing proliferation of pathogenic T cells and microglia
C: Decreased autoimmune and inflammatory attack on motor units
statement: Teriflunomide, an oral MS drug, may limit maladaptive T cell and microglial expansion contributing to motor neuron loss in ALS.

B: Combined β1/α1 adrenoceptor blockade with strong antioxidant activity suppresses microglial oxidative burst and stress kinase activation
C: Lowered oxidative and adrenergic stress, prolonging motor neuron viability
statement: Carvedilol’s triple neuroprotective profile could address microglial hyperactivation and sympathetic dysregulation simultaneously in ALS.

B: Inhibition of human endogenous retrovirus type K integrase reduces HERV-K reverse transcriptase activity and its neurotoxic envelope protein expression
C: Attenuation of retrovirus-induced neuronal toxicity and inflammation, slowing progression
statement: The HIV integrase inhibitor raltegravir could be repositioned to suppress re-activated endogenous retrovirus HERV-K, a suspected neurotoxic driver in ALS.

B: Antagonism of enteric and vagal 5-HT3 receptors dampens gut-derived afferent pro-inflammatory reflex arcs that sustain systemic and neuroinflammation
C: Reduced circulating inflammatory cytokines and delayed motor decline
statement: Alosetron, a 5-HT3 antagonist for IBS, could interrupt the gut-brain inflammatory reflex contributing to ALS progression.
